title: Build labels by joining text with &
summary: Join store codes, article numbers, products and sizes into labels and descriptions with the & operator.

blocks.text: The stock system prints shelf labels from one text field, and the web shop wants a full description for each article. All the parts already exist in separate columns: store, article number, product, colour, size and price.
The & operator joins pieces of text together. In this mission you will build the label and the description from the parts, so that when a size or price changes the text updates by itself.

items: Objective: join cells and fixed text with the & operator.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: The & operator (ampersand) joins its pieces into one piece of text, in order, with nothing added between them. Pieces can be cells, numbers or text in double quotes.
Join the store, a hyphen, the article number, a spaced bar, the product, another spaced bar and the size. For these parts the result is: NBO-0123 | Canvas sneaker | 42

items: Spaces are not added for you. =C2&D2 gives Canvas sneakerwhite. Put the space inside quotes: =C2&" "&D2.
Numbers become text when joined: =1999&"" is the text 1999, which no longer behaves like a number in a lookup.
Leading zeros: an article number such as 0123 must be stored as text (type it with a leading apostrophe, '0123), otherwise Excel keeps only 123.
Tip: write the separator once in your head, then check the result with LEN: a label with a missing space is one character shorter than you expect.

blocks.text: Type numbers without commas or spaces, for example 12.

items: & joins pieces of text; fixed text goes in double quotes.
No spaces or separators are added for you: write them inside the quotes.
Store codes with leading zeros must be text, or the zeros are lost.

blocks.text: Joining by formula keeps labels in step with the data, so a changed size or price never leaves an old label behind.

items.prompt: Cell A2 holds NBO and cell E2 holds 42. What does =A2&" | "&E2 return?
What kind of value does =1999&"" return?
How many characters does the label "NBO-0123 | Canvas sneaker | 42" have? That is, what does =LEN("NBO-0123 | Canvas sneaker | 42") return?
items.answerHint: Whole number, counting spaces and bars

items.prompt: C2 holds Canvas sneaker and D2 holds white. What does =C2&D2 return?
